subject.title: [Feature Request] exec() sandbox isolation and tool permission model — lessons from Claude Code source leak

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for exec sandbox and tool-permission design, or should maintainers supersede it with narrower canonical trackers for sandbox presets, per-tool placement, Codex containment, session lifecycle, and hooks?
rationale: The remaining work defines security boundaries and public config/plugin/runtime contracts, and current main only implements partial opt-in mechanisms.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Milestones
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella while routing implementation into maintainer-owned milestones for each security boundary and compatibility surface.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly designate existing issues such as the sandbox architecture and per-tool placement trackers as the canonical owners for every remaining part.

options.title: Defer Broad Model
options.body: Leave current optional sandboxing and exec approvals as the supported posture for now and document that the broader model is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Milestones
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella while routing implementation into maintainer-owned milestones for each security boundary and compatibility surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from sandbox backend history and prior sandbox architecture review context.
